title: Protect the base of the pawn chain
summary: Support d4 against the c-pawn attack, then develop behind the centre.

fromNode.nodeId: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5

goal: Support d4 against the c-pawn attack, then develop behind the centre.

steps.text: Support the d4 pawn before assuming your space advantage gives an attack.
Develop the king-side knight so it contributes to the centre.
Bring out the bishop and secure the king while watching for more pressure on d4.

jobs.text: Keep the pawn on e5 coordinated with the other pieces; check threats before moving it again.
The pawn controls e5 from here.
The queen controls d4 from here.

opponent.text: The c5 pawn attacks d4. A knight or queen can add pressure, so count attackers and defenders after each new developing move.

notNow: If exchanges have removed the d4 pawn, reassess the new structure instead of following the original chain plan.

mistakes.text: The bishop on h6 can be taken by the pawn on g7. Do not sacrifice a developed piece without a concrete follow-up.

comments.text: Support the d4 pawn with your c-pawn. Black is attacking the base of your pawn chain, so reinforce it before starting a wing attack.

Bring your bishop to e2. It supports your knight on f3.
